messages:
maya: Heads-up — saw a perf regression after yesterday's kernel-selector patch on Llama3-13b. p50 up ~15% on short seqs (<=64) and tail latency spikes.

maya: Quick profiler dump (shortened):
```
Latency p50: 32ms -> 37ms
KV cache miss rate: 2.3% -> 12.1%
Batch sizes: avg 1.8 -> 1.5
Kernel chosen: fused_matmul_v2 -> fallback_matmul
Reason: head_dim mismatch
```

sam: Hmm. fallback_matmul usually indicates selector couldn't match an optimized kernel. Any logs showing head_dim/hidden_size? Could be RMSNorm/SiLU ops not matched.

maya: Paste model meta from onboarding:
```
model: llama-3-13b
hidden_size: 5120
num_heads: 40
head_dim: 128
norm: rmsnorm
activation: silu
rope_theta: 1.0
chat_template: system+user prefix ~320 tokens
```

ryan: But our kernel selector has heuristics that expect head_dim to divide 256/64/32 etc. 128 should be fine. Could the selector be seeing an alternate config (old tokenizer/chat template) forcing different kv stride? Any chance of dynamic padding changing sequence layout so kv cache eviction kicks in?

zara: Also saw prefetch change in the patch: prefetch window reduced from 3->1 for short sequences. That increases cache churn for chat templates with long system prefixes — KV entries get evicted between requests and cause re-computation.

maya: Stack trace from selector:
```
[selector] trying kernels for (hidden=5120, heads=40, head_dim=128)
[selector] candidate fused_matmul_v2: kernel mismatch: expected stride=64, got stride=80
[selector] fallback -> fallback_matmul
```

sam: stride=80 suggests our layout uses 80 bytes per head (maybe float16 + padding). That mismatch could come from quantization profile or an unexpected layout for qkv interleave. Did model conversion step use a nonstandard kv layout? Check model artifact kv_stride metadata.

ryan: Experiment to run:
- force kernel selector to prefer fused_matmul_v2 via env var
- set prefetch_window=3 and pin cache TTL
- run microbench with short sequences and chat template prefix

zara: I'll run a canary with those toggles on a dedicated 1-GPU node and measure p50/p99 + kv miss rate. If kernel choice fixes it then we revert selector heuristics.

perf-bot: Job queued: perf/canary/2847209012 -> node=gpu-a1, config={prefetch:3, selector_force=fused_matmul_v2}

maya: Thanks. Also add telemetry to log 'selector_reason' and 'kv_miss_rate' per request so we can correlate quickly in the future.

sam: One more note — rope_theta defaults historically differed between Llama2 vs Llama3 builds (0.5 vs 1.0). If we accidentally use a mismatched rope config we can get attention interpolation issues but that shouldn't cause kernel mismatch. Still, audit model metadata for rope_theta parity.

maya: Good catch. I'll check artifact metadata + conversion scripts and post results here.

zara: Can we also run a small experiment changing chat template to drop system prefix to see KV churn effect? If latency improves it's probably prefetch/kv eviction not kernel math.

maya: Plan accepted. Will report numbers when perf job finishes. :thumbsup:
